messages:
nina (sales): Heads-up: Pacifica wants a short POC to validate a customer-tuned Llama-50B variant (LoRA integrated) with q4_k style 4-bit quant on Dedicated EU cluster. They need a technical preflight: memory/kv layout for ~64k tokens, p95 latency target <=200ms, and options for KMS or HSM key storage. Also they sent a 15-page security questionnaire. Who can pick up the model compatibility scan + security prefill?
diego (solutions): Ill take the compatibility work. Please upload the model tarball + tokenizer + README explaining the LoRA fusion process. Also we need example prompt traces (long-context and short) and expected concurrency (they mentioned 20qps baseline, spikes to 100qps for 2-3min).
nina (sales): Uploaded to internal transfer: https://files.internal/pacifica/poc-llm50b.tar.gz (link). Tokenizer is a sentencepiece .model. DMed credentials.
ben (eng-runtime): Quick checklist: 1) confirm checkpoint format (hf vs llama-native), 2) verify fused LoRA ordering, 3) run mem footprint estimator to ensure it fits 80GB A100 v5 slice or we need multiple GPUs. Note some q4_k kernels are not available on older runtimes; we can compile kernels in Dedicated but need a day. If HSM is requested for model keys, ops lead needs approval.
li (security): Send the questionnaire here and Ill prefill standard Dedicated answers. HSM will need an ops security review and may require contract addendum. Also need to confirm EU data residency and whether logs contain PII.
molly (finance): Pricing note: Dedicated POC pricing depends on reserved GPU hours. For a ~50B quant model the estimated cost for a 7-day POC at 20qps avg is Y usd (provisional). If they want commit pricing for predictable throughput we can present a short-term reserved bucket. Ill produce two scenarios by EOD.
rahul (cs): Ill reserve eu-central-1 Dedicated slot tomorrow 09:30 CET and invite their engineers for a runbook walkthrough.
diego (solutions): Running our compatibility command once artifacts are local: ```bash
# variant compatibility scan
ri model-scan --source /mnt/pacifica/checkpoint --tokenizer /mnt/pacifica/tokenizer.model --context 65536 --out /tmp/pacificascan.json
```
ben (eng-runtime): Also include a long-context replay test: replay a 60k prefix then append the expected prompt at tail to make sure KV indexes align. If fused-LoRA was applied after quantization, the weight ordering can cause mismatched kv offsets.
li (security): For the SOC2-like Qs we can answer standard controls: encryption-at-rest (yes), KMS key rotation (yes), access logs (yes with 90d retention). Ill flag items needing customer confirmation (e.g., bringing their HSM).
infra-bot: dedicated-cluster:eu-central-1: provisioning started for pacifica-poc-2024-06-12 (id: dc-9123).
rahul (cs): cluster provisioned and SSH jumpbox + temporary creds sent to Pacifica.
nina (sales): Diego/Ben can you post the expected scan ETA? Also can we give Pacifica a short cheat-sheet of what artifacts we need and the timeline?
diego (solutions): ETA 36 hours for full scan + perf regressions. Ill also produce a 1-page "POC artifacts checklist" and a short FAQ covering KMS vs HSM implications, expected timelines, and fallback plan (if 64k not supported we do progressive tests at 8k/32k to measure degradation).
ben (eng-runtime): Noted. If we see attention kernel limits well propose a liveness fallback: reduce kv window + prefix caching to emulate long-context with acceptable latency. That will trade off completeness vs latency.
molly (finance): Shared provisional cost scenarios in the doc: hosted vs dedicated vs short reserved.
li (security): Ill finish the questionnaire prefill and send any redlines. If Pacifica insists on HSM, let legal/ops know - timeline extends by ~2-3 weeks.
nina (sales): Great work team. POC kickoff scheduled 09:30 CET tomorrow. Follow-ups in-thread after the scan. :white_check_mark:
